title: Commutative-square exchange agrees with cohomology pullback on etale charts
statement:
Let $f:X\to Y$, $f':X'\to Y'$, $g:Y'\to Y$, and $g':X'\to X$ be morphisms of schemes [def-pc-scheme] with $fg'=gf'$. No cartesianness is assumed. Let $F$ be an abelian sheaf on $X_{\Et}$ [def-weil-pbc-abelian-etale-sheaves] and $q\geq0$. On the bounded below derived categories [def-weil-pbc-derived-categories], use exact inverse images [def-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image], derived direct images [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], and the adjunctions $f^{-1}\dashv Rf_*$, $f'^{-1}\dashv Rf'_*$ [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction]. Let $E^q:g^{-1}R^qf_*F\to R^qf'_*g'^{-1}F$ be degree-$q$ cohomology of the commutative-square derived exchange [def-kun-commutative-derived-exchange], namely the mate [def-weil-pbc-adjunction-mate] of the inverse-image square isomorphism constructed using $fg'=gf'$ and composition [lem-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-composition]. Here the exact-functor cohomology comparison [lem-weil-pbc-exact-functor-complex-cohomology] identifies $\mathcal H^q(g^{-1}Rf_*F)$ with $g^{-1}R^qf_*F$.
For an etale $U\to Y$ [def-weil-etale-morphism], put $U'=Y'\times_YU$, $T=X\times_YU$, and $T'=X'\times_{Y'}U'$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $t:T'\to T$ be induced by $g'$ and $U'\to U$, and let $F_T$ denote the inverse image of $F$ on $T$. Write $\theta_{f,U}:H^q(T,F_T)\to(R^qf_*F)(U)$ and $\theta_{f',U'}:H^q(T',t^{-1}F_T)\to(R^qf'_*g'^{-1}F)(U')$ for the canonical maps to the sheaves associated to the cohomology presheaves [sbc-lem-higher-direct-image-presheaf], using inverse-image composition identifications. Write $\eta_{g,U}:(R^qf_*F)(U)\to(g^{-1}R^qf_*F)(U')$ for the map on sections induced by the adjunction unit of inverse image [def-weil-pbc-inverse-image]. Then
$$
 E^q(U')\circ\eta_{g,U}\circ\theta_{f,U}
 =\theta_{f',U'}\circ t^*:
 H^q(T,F_T)\longrightarrow(R^qf'_*g'^{-1}F)(U'),
$$
where $H^q$ is etale cohomology [def-weil-pbc-etale-cohomology] and $t^*$ is cohomology pullback [def-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback]. This equality is natural in $F$ and in morphisms of etale test objects $U$.

proof.text: Choose a bounded below complex $I$ of injective abelian sheaves with a quasi-isomorphism $F[0]\to I$, and a bounded below complex $J$ of injectives with a quasi-isomorphism $j:g'^{-1}I\to J$. Enough injectives and the bounded-below representative theorem give the complexes; the K-injective Hom bijection lifts the representing derived isomorphisms to these chain maps. Exactness of $g'^{-1}$ makes the composite $g'^{-1}F[0]\to J$ a quasi-isomorphism, by the natural exact-functor cohomology comparison. Thus $Rf_*F$ and $Rf'_*g'^{-1}F$ are represented by $f_*I$ and $f'_*J$. No injectivity of $g'^{-1}I$ is claimed. All complexes used here are bounded below.

source.place: Tag 0736, lemma-base-change-map-flat-case, first paragraph of the proof; Tag 07A6, lemma-adjoint

proof.text:
Write $\theta^0:f'^{-1}g^{-1}\simeq g'^{-1}f^{-1}$ for the sheaf-level composition isomorphism for the given equality. It is applied termwise on complexes, and its class is the derived square isomorphism by the termwise clause of the derived inverse-image composition theorem. Put $M=g^{-1}f_*I$, $V=g'^{-1}I$ and
$$a=g'^{-1}(\varepsilon_{f,I})\circ\theta^0_{f_*I}:f'^{-1}M\to V,\qquad e=f'_*(j\circ a)\circ\eta_{f',M}:M\to f'_*J.$$
These are chain maps since their components are natural transformations. We verify, rather than assume, that $Q(e)$ represents the specified derived exchange. The derived counits at the bounded below K-injective complexes $I,J$ are the termwise counits by clause (1) of [prop-weil-pbc-derived-inverse-image-adjunction]. The transpose of $Q(e)$ under $f'^{-1}\dashv Rf'_*$ is therefore the class of
$$\varepsilon_{f',J}\circ f'^{-1}e
 =\varepsilon_{f',J}\circ f'^{-1}f'_*(j a)\circ f'^{-1}\eta_{f',M}
 =(j a)\circ\varepsilon_{f',f'^{-1}M}\circ f'^{-1}\eta_{f',M}=j a.$$
The middle equality is counit naturality and the last is the triangle identity. On the other hand the transpose defining exchange is $g'^{-1}(\varepsilon^D_{f,F})\circ\theta^D_{Rf_*F}$, which is the class of $a$, followed by $j$ to identify its target with $QJ$. Injectivity of the adjunction Hom bijection now gives $\operatorname{Ex}_F=Q(e)$ under the resolution identifications. This uses only the specified equality of scheme composites.

proof.text:
We calculate the section map in each complex degree before taking cohomology. For a sheaf $B$ on $X$, let $b_B=g'^{-1}\varepsilon_{f,B}\circ\theta^0_{f_*B}$ and let $\beta^0_B=f'_*(b_B)\circ\eta_{f',g^{-1}f_*B}$. Let $d:f_*g'_*\simeq g_*f'_*$ be the canonical direct-image composition comparison along $fg'=gf'$; on an etale $U\to Y$ it is the identification of evaluations on $X'\times_YU\simeq X'\times_{Y'}(Y'\times_YU)$. To display the adjunction calculation, abbreviate $L=f^{-1}$, $R=f_*$, $L'=f'^{-1}$, $R'=f'_*$, $G=g^{-1}$, $S=g_*$, $H=g'^{-1}$ and $P=g'_*$. Write $\eta^f,\eta^{f'},\eta^g,\eta^{g'}$ for the four sheaf-adjunction units, and $\varepsilon^f$ for the $f$-counit. Thus $d:RP\simeq SR'$ and $\theta^0:L'G\simeq HL$. Clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-inverse-image-composition], applied once to each composite in $fg'=gf'$, gives, for a sheaf $A$ on $Y$,
$$
SR'(\theta^0_A)\circ S(\eta^{f'}_{GA})\circ\eta^g_A
=d_{HLA}\circ R(\eta^{g'}_{LA})\circ\eta^f_A.
$$
Indeed $\theta^0=c_{f,g'}^{-1}c_{g,f'}$ and $d=d_{g,f'}d_{f,g'}^{-1}$, after identifying the equal composite morphisms; substituting the two unit formulas from that clause gives this equality. Put $A=RB$ and expand $\beta^0_B=R'(H\varepsilon^f_B\circ\theta^0_{RB})\circ\eta^{f'}_{GRB}$. Then
$$
\begin{aligned}
S(\beta^0_B)\circ\eta^g_{RB}
&=SR'(H\varepsilon^f_B)\circ SR'(\theta^0_{RB})\circ S(\eta^{f'}_{GRB})\circ\eta^g_{RB}\\
&=SR'(H\varepsilon^f_B)\circ d_{HLRB}\circ R(\eta^{g'}_{LRB})\circ\eta^f_{RB}\\
&=d_{HB}\circ RP(H\varepsilon^f_B)\circ R(\eta^{g'}_{LRB})\circ\eta^f_{RB}\\
&=d_{HB}\circ R(\eta^{g'}_B)\circ R(\varepsilon^f_B)\circ\eta^f_{RB}\\
&=d_{HB}\circ R(\eta^{g'}_B).
\end{aligned}
$$
The successive equalities use the displayed composite-unit identity, naturality of $d$ at $H\varepsilon^f_B$, naturality of $\eta^{g'}$ at $\varepsilon^f_B$, and the triangle identity $R(\varepsilon^f_B)\circ\eta^f_{RB}=1$. This is the horizontal transpose of the underived mate, with no assumption that it is invertible. Applying $f'_*j$ degreewise, evaluating on $U$, and writing $p:T\to X$, $p':T'\to X'$ gives the explicit formula (the fibre-product universal property identifies $X'\times_X T\simeq X'\times_Y U\simeq T'$)
$$e^r(U')\bigl(\eta_{g,f_*I^r}(U)(x)\bigr)=j^r(T')\bigl(\eta_{g',I^r}(T)(x)\bigr),\qquad x\in I^r(T).$$
Under $p^{-1}I^r=I^r|_T$ and $p'^{-1}g'^{-1}I^r\simeq t^{-1}p^{-1}I^r$, the section inside $j^r(T')$ is exactly $\eta_{t,I^r|_T}(T)(x)$. Indeed the two composite units for $pt=g'p'$ agree by the same unit-compatible composition identity, and the units of the etale maps $p,p'$ are restriction. This establishes the actual chart section formula for $e$, including its adjunction-unit factor.

proof.text:
The projections $p:T\to X$ and $p':T'\to X'$ are etale, by the etale base-change statement applied to $U\to Y$ and $U'\to Y'$. Inverse image along them is restriction and preserves injectives (use the constant ring $\mathbf Z$, so these are abelian sheaves). Exactness of restriction preserves the two resolution quasi-isomorphisms. Consequently $I|_T$ and $J|_{T'}$ are bounded below complexes of injectives computing $H^q(T,F_T)$ and $H^q(T',t^{-1}F_T)$, and $j|_{T'}:t^{-1}(I|_T)\to J|_{T'}$ is a resolution comparison. By the definition of cohomology pullback, the chain map
$$w:\Gamma(T,I|_T)\longrightarrow\Gamma(T',J|_{T'}),\qquad w^r(x)=j^r(T')\bigl(\eta_{t,I^r|_T}(x)\bigr)$$
induces exactly $t^*$ on $H^q$. This is the chain map calculated in Step 3. Only the etale projections preserve injectives; $t$ and $g'$ can be arbitrary morphisms.

source.place: Tag 03F3, lemma-cohomology-of-open, restriction of injectives; Tag 0736, resolution comparison

proof.text: For clarity, the passage to sheaves is a quotient calculation. A class $z\in H^q(I(T))$ has a cycle representative $x\in I^q(T)$, with $d(x)=0$. The canonical map $\theta_{f,U}$ sends it to the image of $x$ in $H^q(f_*I)(U)$; this is the canonical map from the cohomology presheaf to its associated sheaf in [sbc-lem-higher-direct-image-presheaf]. Apply the inverse-image unit to this image. Naturality of $\eta_g$ for the cycle inclusion and the cycle-to-cohomology quotient identifies it with the cohomology-sheaf class of $\eta_{g,f_*I^q}(x)$; the exact-functor comparison identifies $H^q(g^{-1}f_*I)$ with $g^{-1}H^q(f_*I)$ and preserves both cycle inclusions and quotient projections. By Step 2, $E^q$ is $H^q(e)$ under that identification. Thus the left side of the required equality at $z$ is the sheaf cohomology class of $e^q(\eta_g(x))=w^q(x)$, by Step 3. Step 4 identifies the raw class of $w^q(x)$ with $t^*z$, whose image in $H^q(f'_*J)(U')$ is $\theta_{f',U'}(t^*z)$. Chain maps carry cycles to cycles and boundaries to boundaries, so this calculation is independent of the chosen representative $x$. It proves the displayed equality for every $z$. We used global cycle representatives only in cohomology of the section complex $I(T)$, not for arbitrary sections of its cohomology sheaf.

source.place: Tag 03Q8, lemma-higher-direct-images, canonical sheafification map; Tag 0736, induced cohomology map

proof.text:
For a morphism $U_1\to U_2$ over $Y$, the fibre-product universal property gives $t_2\circ(T'_1\to T'_2)=(T_1\to T_2)\circ t_1$. The section formula of Step 3 commutes with these restrictions: $j$ is a sheaf map and units and composition comparisons are natural. Taking cycles and their boundary quotients preserves that equality, and the composition clause of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] identifies the resulting raw restriction maps. For a coefficient map $\phi:F\to\widetilde F$, write $s:F[0]\to I$, $\widetilde s:\widetilde F[0]\to\widetilde I$ and $\widetilde j:g'^{-1}\widetilde I\to\widetilde J$ for the chosen resolutions. The K-injective Hom bijection gives chain maps $u:I\to\widetilde I$ and $v:J\to\widetilde J$ representing $\phi$ and $g'^{-1}\phi$. Choose them so $us$ and $\widetilde s\phi$ have the same derived class, and $v j g'^{-1}s$ and $\widetilde j g'^{-1}(\widetilde s\phi)$ have the same derived class. Since $Q(g'^{-1}s)$ is invertible, cancellation gives
$$Q(vj)=Q(\widetilde j\,g'^{-1}u).$$
The target $\widetilde J$ is K-injective, so the same Hom bijection gives a chain homotopy $v j\simeq\widetilde j\,g'^{-1}u$; it does not require $g'^{-1}I$ to be K-injective. Restrict this homotopy to $T'$ and use unit naturality to get
$$v(T')\circ w_I\simeq w_{\widetilde I}\circ u(T).$$
For the exchange representatives, naturality of $\theta^0$, the counit, and the $f'$-unit in Step 2 gives
$$f'_*(v)\circ e\simeq\widetilde e\circ g^{-1}f_*(u).$$
All these are homotopies of actual complexes: additive functors and evaluation preserve a chain-homotopy equation $a-b=dh+hd$. They therefore induce equal cohomology maps. By the morphism clause of [def-weil-pbc-direct-image], $f_*u$ and $f'_*v$ compute the coefficient maps on the higher direct images. The cycle-to-quotient formula in Step 5 commutes with $u,v$, and the exact cohomology comparison is natural; hence both sides of the asserted equation commute with $\phi$. Clauses (1), (3) and (4) of [lem-weil-pbc-cohomology-pullback-functorial] identify these raw maps with the canonical cohomology maps. Taking $\phi=\mathrm{id}$ with two different choices of resolutions proves independence of those choices as well. Thus both stated naturalities hold.
